title: Standard linear action on scheme-theoretic projective space
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $I$ a finite set. Write $H=\operatorname{GL}_{I,k}$ [def-sc-general-linear-group], a group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], $C=k[H]$, and $P=\operatorname{Proj}(k[z_i:i\in I])$ with total-degree grading [def-pc-proj] [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], regarded as the projective space of lines in $k^I$. Put $\delta:k[z_i]\to C[z_i]$, fixing base coefficients and sending $z_i$ to $\sum_j x_{ij}z_j$. An action $a:H\times_k P\to P$, satisfying the identity and associativity diagrams, is the standard linear projective action if, under the canonical affine-base-change isomorphism $\operatorname{Proj}(C[z_i])\simeq H\times_k P$ [def-pc-fibre-product], its action map is $\operatorname{Proj}(\delta)$. The first projection of this isomorphism is the structure morphism to $H=\operatorname{Spec}C$, and the second is $\operatorname{Proj}$ of the coefficient extension fixing all $z_i$. These projection formulas determine the comparison uniquely. The coordinate substitution and all equalities concern scheme morphisms, so include arbitrary nonreduced test algebras.
